Remaining ways to defeat the new rule (О39; design section 23): (1) a forged or edited REQ-VALIDATOR handoff with an earlier completed_at and verdict PASS naming the requirement — FIRSTGATE and checks (4), (5) trust the handoffs; the defense is the append-only handoffs, handoffs-check and ORCH's step checks; (2) a form row inserted BEFORE the real first gate row, naming a real but later PASS handoff (V28e) — the rule takes it; check (5) (CD-4) is red on a table built from it, (1) and (4) on the built table; (3) a missing or misspelled form row («Gate PASS:», leading text) for a newly gated requirement — it is left out of the table; check (6) is red at S1 and step 9 while it is pending, in progress or blocked; (4) a program requirement numbered below REQ-102 — check (6) covers REQ-102 on only (program plan §4.2).

GATESEQ in CD-2 is its durable part only: every gate line is exactly a row name of the gate table (V09c red). The equal part (the gate lines equal the unanswered rows) is not in the permanent test on purpose: an owner's answer recorded in PROGRESS.md would turn npm run check red until the next run refreshes the block; rule 5.5 makes every writer check equality when it writes. If ORCH reads О38 as the equal part in CD-2, that coupling (an answer -> a red check until the refresh) is the price.
